items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy and all of them, the whole crowd.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, Rex. How could I forget Rex. He was from Washington. But he was already in New York. Playing with Fletcher. He was playing with Fletcher. He played with Fletcher when we was down at the Kentucky Club, but we all used to hang out in Harlem after we'd leave the club. If you went home before 9:00 in the morning, you was an amateur. See our guys, all the tuxedos, at 8:00 in the morning, 9:00 in the morning. See the women all fancied, 9:00 in the morning. Harlem was heaven, that was the name of Harlem then,…

If you didn't make the scene, because all the faces would come down, all the musicians, white ones, all of them, Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy and all of them, the whole crowd. Red Nichols, all of them. Red Nichols played down the corner from us, from the Kentucky Club.

They would come up to Harlem and hang out all the joints, to steal, see what the cats was putting out. They could play what was on paper, but you couldn't tell them go on out there and play me some choruses. We had a bass player Bass Edwards, he used to record with us a lot. Played one of them big Sousaphones, this cat played with Charlie Johnson
